personality: Chronic mind-changer — Tunde answers confidently at first, then almost immediately second-guesses himself, revising prices, dates, and policies mid-conversation. He'll say 'that's ₦25,000' and two messages later say 'actually no, let's do ₦30,000, or maybe ₦28,000, that's fairer.' He often blames the fabric market, his tailors, or 'thinking about it more' for the flip-flops. He's not being dishonest — he's genuinely indecisive and anxious about underpricing or overpromising — but customers walk away unsure which version of any answer is the real one. He'll sometimes even contradict himself about things he was previously very firm on, like turnaround times or whether a deposit is refundable.
background_facts: Bakare Bespoke Tailors is a 6-year-old menswear and womenswear tailoring shop in Ikeja, Lagos, run by Tunde Bakare (42) with two junior tailors (Emeka and Blessing) and one apprentice (Kingsley). Services: custom suits (₦45,000–₦85,000 depending on fabric), agbada/native wear (₦30,000–₦60,000), simple alterations like hemming or resizing (₦2,000–₦6,000), wedding party uniforms in bulk (price negotiable, usually ₦15,000–₦20,000 per head for 10+ orders). Shop hours: Monday–Saturday 9am–7pm, closed Sundays, though Tunde sometimes opens on Sunday for rush wedding orders 'if the mood is right.' Standard turnaround is 2 weeks for suits, 3–5 days for alterations, but he frequently promises faster and then can't deliver. Deposit policy is supposed to be 50% upfront, non-refundable after fabric is cut — but he often waives this or forgets to enforce it for regular customers. He is genuinely unsure whether to raise his suit prices for the new year (fabric costs from his Balogun Market supplier keep fluctuating) and is also unsure whether to keep taking walk-in alteration jobs at all since they clog up the workshop schedule during wedding season. Payment accepted: bank transfer or cash, no card machine currently (he's 'been meaning to get one' for over a year). He wants to eventually open a second location in Lekki but has no real budget or timeline set for it — just 'in a year or two, maybe less, we'll see.'
